newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Weak Irish bonds shrug off strong U.S. data.
newsitem.headline: Weak Irish bonds shrug off strong U.S. data.

text.p: Irish bonds drifted off in moderate trade on Friday, largely ignoring stronger-than-expected U.S. non-farm payroll data.
Dealers said turnover in Irish paper was not huge and trade was mainly confined to domestic players.

"The main focus for all markets was the U.S. data and although it came in higher than expected there were conflicting signals in the figures so we have seen a mixed reaction in bond markets," one dealer said.
Data released by the U.S. Labour Department on Friday showed that the non-farm payrolls grew by 339,000 jobs in February, exceeding economists' forecasts of 230,000.

The unemployment rate returned to its 5.3 percent prevailing trend, offering relief to bond investors who had feared a drop to 5.2 percent from January's 5.4 percent, a fall that would have been read as a sign of a very tight labour market.

''After the (U.S.) figures came out there were a lot of people asking about prices but it did not translate into much activity in the Irish market,'' a dealer said. ''Once the bunds settled down, things settled down in Dublin.''

By 1600 GMT, the 6.5 percent bond due 2001 was down 20 pence from Thursday's close to 102.00 to yield 5.98 percent while the key benchmark eight percent bond due 2006 shed 10 pence from the close to 109.60 to yield 6.60 percent.
Earlier a routine council meeting by Bundesbank members resulted in the repo rate being left unchanged at a fixed 3.0 percent. -- Dublin newsroom 353-1-660-3377
